history.america-difference.0041.all: 1861: enslaved people legally property, no freedom, under owners' control, Fugitive slave laws; 1865: freed by 13th Amendment (Dec 1865)/Emancipation Proclamation 1863, Union advance, Freedmen's Bureau, could move/reunite families, serve as USCT soldiers.

history.america-difference.0052.all: 1865: freed but with little land/rights, Black Codes, Freedmen's Bureau just set up; 1870: 14th (1868) and 15th (1870) amendments gave citizenship and vote, Black men voting/holding office, sharecropping emerging, KKK violence.

history.america-difference.0012.all: 1783: slavery legal/entrenched in most Northern states, little organised opposition (only Vermont/Massachusetts/Pennsylvania starting); by 1804 all Northern states had abolished or begun gradual abolition (NJ 1804), abolition societies, Northwest Ordinance 1787 banned slavery; 1808 slave trade ban looming.

history.america-difference.0059.all: 1868: Treaty of Fort Laramie, army withdrew from Bozeman Trail forts, Sioux gained Black Hills/Great Sioux Reservation, relatively peaceful; 1876: gold in Black Hills (1874), army sent to force Sioux onto reservations, Great Sioux War, Little Bighorn June 1876, full conflict.

history.america-judgement.0012.all: Plan: Yes significant: exposed weakness of Articles (no army, no taxes), alarmed elites -> Philadelphia Convention 1787 -> Constitution with stronger federal govt, standing army. But other factors: Northwest Ordinance, Hamilton's financial plan, Washington, Whiskey Rebellion 1794 showing federal power; Louisiana Purchase. Conclude significant catalyst but not sole factor.

history.america-judgement.0023.all: Plan: Conflict: Mexico 1846-48, Texas annexation, Native American wars/removal, War of 1812 earlier, Oregon dispute with Britain. But other consequences: sectional tension over slavery (Missouri 1820, Wilmot Proviso, Compromise 1850, Kansas-Nebraska 1854), economic growth, Native removal, population shift. Argue slavery sectionalism arguably more important/long term.

history.america-judgement.0039.all: Plan: Blockade (Anaconda Plan) cut cotton exports, shortages, inflation, but porous early and leaky; other factors: Northern industrial/population superiority, Grant/Sherman total war, Vicksburg/Gettysburg 1863, Emancipation and Black soldiers, Confederate poor finances/states' rights. Judge blockade important but contributory.

history.america-judgement.0061.all: Plan: Sharecropping after 1865-ish gave some independence from gang labour but trapped in debt, crop lien, cycle of poverty; other changes: 13th-15th Amendments, Freedmen's Bureau schools, political participation, Black Codes, KKK, end of Reconstruction 1877. Conclude sharecropping important to economic life but political/legal changes also major.

history.america-judgement.0012.problem: minor: 2nd stimulus bullet (stronger federal government) is really the Constitution, which the mark scheme also lists as an 'other factor'
history.america-judgement.0012.fix: optional: reword bullet to 'The Constitutional Convention of 1787'

history.america-judgement.0039.problem: Stimulus bullet 'He kept the border states in the Union' has no antecedent and is not about the blockade; the mark scheme treats it as the opposing factor 'leadership of Lincoln'.
history.america-judgement.0039.fix: Replace with a blockade-relevant bullet (e.g. 'The Anaconda Plan') and keep Lincoln's leadership as an own-knowledge factor.

history.america-judgement.0061.problem: Stimulus bullet 'It abolished slavery in 1865' is not about sharecropping and 'It' is unclear (Thirteenth Amendment); mark scheme treats Thirteenth Amendment as an opposing factor.
history.america-judgement.0061.fix: Replace with a sharecropping-relevant bullet (e.g. 'Debt to landowners and merchants') and keep the Thirteenth Amendment as an own-knowledge factor.
